topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability defines likelihood given known info.
P(A|B) is probability of A given B occurred.
Sample space shrinks to region of B.
animations: Fade in text 'Conditional Probability: P(A|B) = P(A∩B) / P(B)'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate circle representing event B. Color: #FF0000.
Animate intersection area A∩B inside B. Color: #00FF00.
Highlight formula P(A|B) while fading other components.
Transition to next scene with summary box.

sections.title: Defining Independence
lecture_lines: Events are independent if B gives no A info.
Independent events do not influence each other.
animations: Fade in two separate boxes for events A and B. Color: #FFFF00.
Show intersection size changing as events become independent.

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversal
lecture_lines: It updates prior beliefs with new evidence.
Prior probability evolves into posterior probability.
Used to diagnose rare events accurately.
animations: Display Bayes' Theorem formula: 'P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A) / P(B)'. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show P(A) and P(B) as distinct probability bars. Color: #00FFFF.
Animate 'Reversal' by swapping positions of A and B.
Highlight P(B|A) in the formula. Color: #FF00FF.

sections.title: Synthesis and Practical Application
lecture_lines: Decision trees visualize Bayesian updating processes.
AI filters apply this to identify spam.
animations: Display real-world problem statement box. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show data points being added to a graph. Color: #00FF00.
